rejected: The paper identifies a specific product vendor.
The comparison proves the artificial intelligence tool can't improve hospital outcomes.
The case-manager estimates and artificial intelligence estimates were tested under equivalent workflow conditions.
Greater discharge-date accuracy in this study establishes better downstream clinical decisions or patient outcomes.
required_edits_applied: The admission panel assigns 4.27 days to case managers and 4.20 days to artificial intelligence, matching the cited result.
The opening identifies Houston and the September 3rd publication date without inventing a study or implementation date.
The workflow caveat shows that case-manager estimates were visible to care teams while artificial intelligence estimates were available in the record but not enabled automatically.
The ending limits the finding to estimation accuracy and calls for the prospective outcome-based test the authors say is still needed.
The film names no unsupported product vendor and makes no claim that either estimate improved patient outcomes.
